message.content: The sea’s color isn’t fixed—it changes with depth, light, and what’s in the water. In shallow, clear waters you’ll often see a bright turquoise or aquamarine hue. As the depth increases, the water absorbs longer wavelengths (reds, oranges) and reflects shorter ones (blues), so deeper parts look more blue or even indigo. Near the surface, sunlight can scatter and give the sea a pale blue or even a greenish tint if there’s algae or plankton. So, while “blue” is the most common description, the sea can range from turquoise to deep navy, depending on conditions.
